description:
Spec commit `80d5e11` (2026-05-11) dropped five aggregate-count cap-advertising fields from `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat`:

- `maxGroupMembers`
- `maxSpaceMembers`
- `maxRolesPerSpace`
- `maxChannelsPerSpace`
- `maxCategoriesPerSpace`

Per-aggregate enforcement now uses the standard `overQuota` SetError (RFC 8620 §5.3) at exceed time. Account-level visibility is recommended via JMAP Quotas (RFC 9425) as a SHOULD. The three remaining per-message caps (`maxBodyBytes`, `maxAttachmentBytes`, `maxAttachmentsPerMessage`) were kept because they have RFC 8621 analogs in `urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail`.

This bead closes the spec-side bead `JMAP-kt5k` from the workspace side.

## Tasks

### Task A: `jmap-chat-client` — drop fields from `ChatCapability`

File: `crate-jmap-chat-client/src/session.rs`

- Lines 25–41: remove the five Rust fields (`max_group_members`, `max_space_members`, `max_roles_per_space`, `max_channels_per_space`, `max_categories_per_space`) from `ChatCapability`. Keep `max_body_bytes`, `max_attachment_bytes`, `max_attachments_per_message`, `supports_threads`, `extra`, and any other unchanged field.
- Test `chat_capability_parses` (line ~290): remove the five lines from the JSON fixture (`"maxGroupMembers": 100,` etc. at lines 304–308) and the five corresponding `cap.max_*` assertions (lines 326–330).
- Test `chat_capability_preserves_vendor_extras` (line ~380): remove the five lines from its JSON fixture (lines 385–389). The test's oracle is `acmeCorpFeatureFlag` round-trip, so removing the dropped fields does not weaken it.

Note: the struct is `#[non_exhaustive]` with a `serde_json::Map` `extra` flatten catch-all per workspace extras-preservation policy. Once the typed fields are removed, any client receiving a server that still emits the dropped names will harmlessly land them in `extra` — no round-trip data loss.

### Task B: `jmap-chat-server` — fix stale doc comment

File: `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs`

Lines 168–169 currently read (inside the doc comment on `apply_space_patch`):

> Handler-side permission gates (`manage_space`, `manage_roles`, `manage_members`, `manage_channels`) and add-op count limits (`maxRolesPerSpace`, `maxSpaceMembers`, `maxChannelsPerSpace`, `maxCategoriesPerSpace`) are tracked in `bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.7` and `bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8` and are NOT yet applied by the reference handler.

Reword so it no longer cites the dropped spec-field names (which are now implementation-defined). Suggested replacement, preserving the bead references:

> Handler-side permission gates (`manage_space`, `manage_roles`, `manage_members`, `manage_channels`) and per-aggregate count limits on roles, members, channels, and categories per Space are tracked in `bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.7` and `bd:JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8` and are NOT yet applied by the reference handler. When applied, exceed-limit cases return `overQuota` SetError (RFC 8620 §5.3) per draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/set.

## Verification

```bash
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

`cargo test -p jmap-chat-client` must pass — specifically `chat_capability_parses` and `chat_capability_preserves_vendor_extras`. No other tests should be affected.

## Out of scope

- `JMAP-g7wu.2.4.8` (count-limit enforcement implementation) — separate bead, unchanged in shape by this spec edit.
- `jmap-chat-types` — unaffected; the capability struct does not live there.
- `jmap-filenode-*` — the filenode spec was also edited today (`b1e639b`) but it was a pure bibliography reference update (draft-ietf-jmap-quotas → RFC 9425) with no Rust impact.
- Workspace `AGENTS.md` past-tensing of the `JMAP-kt5k` reference — handled directly in this session, no separate bead.
title: Workspace catch-up to spec commit 80d5e11 (drop 5 cap-advertising fields from ChatCapability)
